data_points.notes: India ayurvedic SKINCARE only — facial care, body care, hair and scalp care, specialty (anti-ageing, acne). This is the cleanest BPC-scoped ayurvedic figure found; it does NOT cover ayurvedic oral care or colour cosmetics, so it under-covers the ayurvedic_herbal adjacency as a whole. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated on this page; note the same publisher's all-ayurvedic page puts organised at 70% / unorganised at 30% in 2025, and the ayurvedic personal-care tail (loose oils, regional herbal brands) is heavily unorganised.

IMARC: India ayurvedic skincare USD 2.0bn (2025) to USD 5.8bn (2034), CAGR 11.98% 2026-2034. SCOPE CAVEAT: ayurvedic skincare only, not the full ayurvedic/herbal BPC adjacency. cf the same publisher's all-ayurvedic-products CAGR of 15.52% — but that basket is 58% healthcare (medicines and nutraceuticals), which is outside BPC, so the two are not comparable and must not be averaged. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated.

data_points.methodology: Ayurvedic PERSONAL CARE size derived from two figures stated on the same fetched IMARC page: India ayurvedic products INR 1,017.51 Billion (2025), of which 'healthcare products dominate the market with a share of 58% in 2025'. Personal care is therefore the residual 42%: 1,017.51bn x 0.42 = INR 427.35bn = INR 42,735 Crore, ~USD 4.44bn at the pinned rate USD/INR 96.23 (config/exchange_rates.yaml, pinned 2026-07-21). Sensitivity: at a 40-45% personal-care share the range is INR 40,700-45,788 Crore (USD 4.23-4.76bn). Cross-check: Sourceready's India herbal & ayurvedic beauty report states USD 4.5-5.2bn for 2025 — consistent with the top of this range, but that page cites no original source for the figure so it is not recorded as a claim.
data_points.notes: IMARC's ayurvedic personal-care scope is skin care, oral care, hair care and fragrances — wider than the ayurvedic skincare figure of USD 2.0bn (2025) from the same publisher, which is why this estimate is roughly 2.2x it. ORGANISED/UNORGANISED: the source page states organised leads with 70% share in 2025, so unorganised is ~30% and IS included in the base. Derived, not published — do not cite as a source figure.

IMARC: India ayurvedic products INR 1,017.51bn (2025) to INR 3,728.75bn (2034), CAGR 15.52% 2026-2034 (~USD 10.57bn to ~USD 38.75bn at the pinned rate USD/INR 96.23, config/exchange_rates.yaml pinned 2026-07-21). HARD SCOPE CAVEAT: 58% of this basket is healthcare products (ayurvedic medicines and nutraceuticals), which are OUTSIDE BPC scope — this growth rate is majority-driven by non-BPC demand and should not be applied to the BPC ayurvedic/herbal adjacency. Kept only because the derived personal-care market_size claim uses the same base. Organised 70% / unorganised 30% in 2025, so both are covered. cf ayurvedic-skincare-only 11.98%.

India halal cosmetics, USD 1.3bn (2025). Scope covers personal care (skin, hair, fragrances, other) plus colour cosmetics (face, eye, lip, nail). Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. SCOPE CAVEAT: halal certification in India is issued by private bodies with no single national register, so what counts as 'halal certified' is publisher-defined and unauditable.

IMARC: India halal cosmetics USD 1.3bn (2025) to USD 2.5bn (2034), CAGR 7.28% 2026-2034. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. Note MarkNtel publishes a much higher India halal cosmetics growth figure (~30% CAGR per its press-release headline) — that page was not fetched and is therefore not recorded as a claim, but the spread signals the cell is unreliable.

India clean beauty INR 7,786.49 Crore (2025), ~USD 0.81bn at the pinned rate USD/INR 96.23 (config/exchange_rates.yaml, pinned 2026-07-21). Scope: skin care (face and body), hair care, colour cosmetics. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated — 'clean beauty' is a branded-claim category so unorganised trade is almost certainly excluded in practice. SCOPE CAVEAT: 'clean' is a marketing claim with no Indian regulatory definition, so the boundary is publisher-defined.

EMR: India clean beauty INR 7,786.49 Crore (2025) to INR 33,471.51 Crore (2035), CAGR 15.70% 2026-2035 (~USD 0.81bn to ~USD 3.48bn at the pinned rate USD/INR 96.23, pinned 2026-07-21). Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. SCOPE CAVEAT: 'clean' has no Indian regulatory definition; boundary is publisher-defined.

SCOPE CAVEAT: IMARC's 'beauty devices' basket is dominated by small electrical grooming appliances — trimmers & shavers, hair dryers, straighteners, curlers, epilators, face cleansers, others. That is a personal-care appliance market, NOT the at-home skincare-device adjacency (LED masks, microcurrent, cleansing brushes) the taxonomy sub-segment targets. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. cf TechSci USD 1.81bn (2024) on the identical seven-category scope — broadly consistent.

SCOPE CAVEAT: same seven-category appliance scope as IMARC (trimmers & shavers, hair dryers, straighteners, curlers, epilators, face cleanser, others) — personal-care appliances rather than at-home skincare devices. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. cf IMARC USD 2.1bn (2025) — consistent given one year of growth, unusually so for a pair of aggregators.

IMARC: USD 2.1bn (2025) to USD 7.4bn (2034), CAGR 14.56% 2026-2034. SCOPE CAVEAT: personal-care appliance basket, see the matching market_size claim. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. cf TechSci 15.56% to 2030 — the two agree closely.

TechSci: USD 1.81bn (2024) to USD 4.31bn (2030), CAGR 15.56%. SCOPE CAVEAT: personal-care appliance basket. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. cf IMARC 14.56% (2026-2034) — close agreement, unusual for aggregator pairs and a mild positive signal on this cell.

[CORRIDOR] India K-beauty products market, USD 310mn (2025), forecast USD 872mn by 2032. Page also states facial skincare is ~65% of the K-beauty mix and female consumers ~80%. It cites India BPC at USD 28bn (2024) but does NOT compute K-beauty's share of that, so no share figure is claimed here. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated; grey-market and parallel-import K-beauty is a known unmeasured channel in India, so this likely undercounts sell-through. cf Credence Research USD 406.58mn (2023) — Credence's EARLIER-year level EXCEEDS this LATER-year level on a growing category, a direct contradiction; definitional mismatch unresolved, do not average.

[CORRIDOR] India K-beauty product market, USD 406.58mn (2023), forecast USD 959.33mn by 2032. Organised/unorganised coverage not stated; grey-market/parallel-import K-beauty is a known and unmeasured channel in India, so any of these figures likely undercounts actual sell-through. cf MarkNtel USD 310mn (2025) — MarkNtel's later-year figure is 24% BELOW this earlier-year figure; the two cannot both be right, definitional mismatch unresolved, do not average.

[CORRIDOR] MarkNtel: India K-beauty CAGR 18.06% 2026-2032 (USD 310mn 2025 to USD 872mn 2032). Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. cf Credence Research 10.00% 2024-2032 — a 1.8x gap on the growth rate on top of a contradictory size base; definitional mismatch unresolved, do not average.

[CORRIDOR] Credence: India K-beauty CAGR 10.00% 2024-2032 (USD 406.58mn 2023 to USD 959.33mn 2032). Organised/unorganised coverage not stated. cf MarkNtel 18.06% 2026-2032 — 1.8x gap, and the two size bases contradict each other outright; definitional mismatch unresolved, do not average.
